title: Bounded flat inverse-image complexes compute all target-side tensor tests
statement:
Let $f:V\to X$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the constant ring sheaves $A_X,A_V$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their canonical inverse image $f_A^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $c\leq d$ be integers and let $P$ be a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] of flat $A_X$-module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] with $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[c,d]$. Write $Q(P)$ for its image in the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $D(f_A^*)$ for the functor induced by termwise inverse image, which is exact [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact].

The termwise complex $f_A^*P$ has flat $A_V$-module terms, is zero outside $[c,d]$, and is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There is a natural isomorphism $Q(f_A^*P)\cong D(f_A^*)Q(P)$. For every $A_V$-module sheaf $M$ placed in degree zero, with no assumption that $M$ is pulled back from $X$, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
$$D(f_A^*)Q(P)\otimes_A^L M\cong Q((f_A^*P)\otimes_{A_V}M),$$
using derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. The complex on the right is zero outside $[c,d]$; consequently the left side has zero cohomology in every degree outside $[c,d]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. No constructibility, Noetherianity or etaleness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: A finite commutative ring is Noetherian. In the fixed-ring ModuleCat-valued presentation, exactness of tensorRight is equivalent by the braiding to the two-sided flatness ObjectProperty.flat. Apply the existing fixed-scalar pro-etale pullback flatness instance upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat to each term. This is the same inverse image appearing in termwisePullback, and requires no condition on f.

The existing upperStar is additive and exact, as recorded by its preserved finite limits and colimits instances. Its additive structure preserves zero objects, so apply map_isZero to the original interval bounds. Restrict mapDerivedCategoryFactors.symm along the full subcategory inclusion to obtain the natural termwise localization comparison; there is no boundedness premise for this comparison.

The preserved upper bound gives IsStrictlyLE d for the pulled-back complex. Apply the existing generic monoidal-category criterion CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat with the flat terms from step 1. The Grothendieck abelian sheaf category has the exact integer-indexed colimits and tensor colimit preservation required by that criterion. This proves the actual two-sided quasi-isomorphism K-flatness predicate of the statement directly.

Use the canonical lax monoidal tensorator of DerivedCategory.Q, restricted along the pulled-back complex functor and the degree-zero single functor. Its naturality in both variables is exactly LaxMonoidal.mu_natural. For a K-flat first complex, pass its K-flatness to the homotopy category; DerivedMonoidal.isIso_counit_app_app_of_kFlat_left makes the Qh tensorator invertible. The tensorator of Q is transported along quotientCompQhIso and is the composite of tensor products of isomorphisms, the Qh tensorator, the localized monoidal quotient tensorator, and quotientCompQhIso. Hence every component is invertible. Package it with asIso and compose with the inverse of the factorization comparison in the first variable. The private helpers tensorComparison, isIsoQTensor and tensorTestsIso carry out these generic operations without exposing large sheaf constructions. The second complex is arbitrary, so no descent hypothesis on M is used. The public implementation helper tensorTestFunctor constructs exactly the product followed by the uncurry of the tensor functor; strictTests and derivedTests share it. Its generic tensorTestFunctorComparison proves the comparison before concrete sheaf specialization, avoiding repeated kernel expansion. Both test functors remain definitionally equal to their original constructions. The proved private sheafQTensorIsIso checks the tensorator in the symbolic coefficient category first; its specialization has exactly the canonical fixed-ring tensorator.

proof.text: The source-library mapBifunctorSingle2Iso identifies the signed tensor with M[0] with the complex obtained by applying tensorRight M termwise. Apply map_isZero to the preserved interval bounds and evaluate this chain isomorphism in degree n, obtaining strict term vanishing. A short complex with zero middle object has zero homology, so the strict test has zero homology in that degree. Finally transport along homologyFunctor applied to the natural derived-test comparison, followed by homologyFunctorFactors. This proves the required derived cohomology vanishing, including for completely arbitrary target module sheaves.

The five steps match main-20261015 thm-exc-explicit-preservation proof paragraph 2 and unit step 3. Step 1: the ringed-topos flat-pullback lemma (Stacks 05VD, checked) applies to f_proet, which is a geometric morphism by lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor. Its u^*F is literally the module pullback of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, and no flatness of c is assumed. Step 2: prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact needs only a finite ring and an arbitrary morphism. Its commutative clause, together with prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, identifies its functor with f_A^*. The exact-functor factorization (Stacks 015F) gives Q(f^*P) ≅ D(f^*)Q(P) with no resolution. Step 3: sites-cohomology lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat is Tag 06YQ (checked in tags/tags); the bound d comes from step 2 and flatness from step 1. Step 4: the identity map is a K-flat resolution of the first factor in def-weil-derived-tensor's order. Resolution independence gives the canonical, natural identification, M is never resolved, and naturality is written out explicitly. Step 5 (elementary): Tot(F⊗M[0])^n = F^n⊗M, so the complex is zero outside [c,d]. Edge cases checked: V empty, A=0, c=d, A=Z/4 with M=Z/2, f=id. Overlaps checked: lem-sp-proetale-ctf-pullback-domains is only a finite-type, constructible special case. The four tool_uses are generic tools on the unit's route and are accepted. lean.statement: theorem bounded_flat_pullback_test {V X : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ X) (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (c d : ℤ) (_hcd : c ≤ d) : (∀ P : (flatInterval X A c d).FullSubcategory, (∀ q : ℤ, exactFunctor _ _ (tensorRight (((termwisePullback f A).obj P.obj).X q))) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < c ∨ d < q → IsZero (((termwisePullback f A).obj P.obj).X q)) ∧ (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)).kFlat ((termwisePullback f A).obj P.obj)) ∧ Nonempty ((flatInterval X A c d).ι ⋙ termwisePullback f A ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ (flatInterval X A c d).ι ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).mapDerivedCategory) ∧ Nonempty (derivedTests f A c d ≅ strictTests f A c d ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) ∧ ∀ (P : (flatInterval X A c d).FullSubcategory) (M : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (n : ℤ), n < c ∨ d < n → IsZero (((strictTests f A c d).obj (P, M)).X n) ∧ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj ((derivedTests f A c d).obj (P, M)))
